winner.title: Ropa Vieja Recipe

evidence.authenticity: Flank steak braised with onion, peppers, tomato, cumin, oregano, allspice, white wine, olives, served with rice and beans; classic Cuban profile. Streamlined one-pot method, not a traditional two-pot boil-then-sofrito. Author is not Cuban.
evidence.precision: Weights for 10 of 19 ingredients (e.g. onion 415g, peppers 250g each); 11 sensory cues in steps (shimmering oil, browned, very tender, thin long shreds, glaze coats beef); oven temp 350F; Dutch oven but no pan size.
evidence.testing: Serious Eats test kitchen; description explains why the one-pot approach gives better beefy flavor, and a note on cuts. Only 4 ratings (3.8), so little user validation.
evidence.photos: 3 step images in schema (vegetables, braise assembly, shredding); page has more images.
evidence.efficiency: Single pot, 10 min prep, 2 hr cook; stated 2h10m is realistic.
evidence.access: All ingredients at a US grocery.

winner.why: Beat ATK on precision (weights for more than half the ingredients, a doneness cue at nearly every step) and on visible process photos.

runnerUp.title: Ropa Vieja (Cuban Braised Shredded Beef)

evidence.authenticity: Cuban flavor base, but uses brisket instead of flank and adds anchovy for depth, so it departs from tradition.
evidence.precision: No weights (volume and count only); strip widths given (2-inch, 1/4-inch shreds); 10 sensory cues; 300F oven; Dutch oven size not given.
evidence.testing: ATK test kitchen; rating 4.6 from 90 ratings; description explains the choice of cut for texture.
evidence.photos: Step photos hidden behind login; not marked down for that (scored 10).
evidence.efficiency: Two dense steps, about 3 hours total; sensible.
evidence.access: Anchovy and brisket are available at US grocery stores.

runnerUp.why: Strong testing and a 4.6 rating, but less precise on quantities and less traditional than the Serious Eats version.

candidates.disqualified: Mexican poblano and flour tortilla version, not Cuban ropa vieja

notes: Kenji's NYT version (4.0 from 1526 ratings) adds raisins and capers and needs a separate peppers-and-onions sub-recipe. Laylita has good step photos but few doneness cues and no ratings. No candidate was from a Cuban author.
